one_liner: Pure-Haskell Unicode NFC/NFKC/NFD/NFKD normalization for Text, beating ICU's C library binding on decomposition forms.
what_it_does: Normalizes Data.Text values to NFC, NFKC, NFD, or NFKD form entirely in Haskell, avoiding the FFI call into the native ICU4C library that text-icu uses. The whole API is one function, `normalize :: NormalizationMode -> Text -> Text` in Data.Text.Normalize, plus a deprecated ByteString-based variant kept for legacy callers. It is a functional substitute for text-icu's normalization, not a drop-in replacement: call sites must switch to this function signature.
how_it_is_fast: It rides text's internal stream-fusion machinery (Data.Text.Internal.Fusion) to decompose/recompose characters while writing directly into a mutable Text array, avoiding intermediate list or Text allocations. Combining marks awaiting reorder by combining class are held in a small hand-unrolled buffer (`ReBuf = Empty | One Char | Many Char Char [Char]`) rather than a general list, so the common 0-2 mark case avoids list overhead. Hangul syllable decomposition/composition is done algorithmically instead of via UCD table lookup. The library is built with `-O2 -funbox-strict-fields -fspec-constr-count=10` (optional LLVM backend via a cabal flag).
when_to_use: Pure-Haskell codebases that want to drop the native ICU4C runtime dependency and FFI overhead of text-icu
Decomposition-heavy workloads (NFD/NFKD): wins all 14 measured README rows, from +8.8% to +377% over ICU
Batch/offline normalization of in-memory Data.Text values, e.g. Korean or Vietnamese text (largest measured wins)
Projects on GHC 8.0.2 through 9.14.1 wanting a small dependency footprint (base, text, bytestring, ghc-prim, unicode-data only)
Cases where a small, auditable pure-Haskell implementation is preferred over linking libicu
when_not_to_use: Composition-heavy workloads (NFC/NFKC): ICU is faster in 9 of 14 measured rows, e.g. NFC/Japanese 11.90ms vs ICU's 3.04ms, NFC/AllChars 9.72ms vs 3.58ms
NFKC on Korean input specifically: open issue #106 reports NFKC is not idempotent on some Korean inputs — a correctness bug, not just a perf gap
Need ICU features beyond normalization (collation, FCD normalization, string iteration, regex) — this package does normalization only
Callers outside Haskell (C/C++/other languages) — there is no exposed FFI surface, it's a Haskell library only

Need normalization numbers you can trust on your own hardware: the published table is for package v0.3.7 (current is 0.4.0.1), unspecified 'macOS' hardware with no CPU model, GHC version, compiler flags, or run date given

integration.dependencies: base (>=4.8,<4.23), text (>=1.1.1,<=1.2.5.0 or >=2.0,<2.2), bytestring, ghc-prim, unicode-data
integration.platforms: any (pure Haskell); CI covers Linux, Windows (AppVeyor), and s390x
integration.thread_safety: not documented (pure, allocation-based functions; no stated concurrency caveats)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: same underlying Data.Text type and no native ICU dependency, but the API (Data.Text.Normalize.normalize) differs from text-icu's interface, so call sites must be rewritten

gotchas: Open bug: NFKC is not idempotent on some Korean inputs (issue #106, still open as of 2026-08-17)
Ships a deprecated Data.ByteString.UTF8.Normalize module alongside the current Data.Text.Normalize API
For some scripts (Japanese, AllChars) composition forms are markedly slower than ICU, up to roughly 4x, not just a modest loss
Package is still marked 'Experimental' stability in its cabal file despite a decade of releases
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The catalogued siblings are C/C++/Rust/Go SIMD UTF-8 validators/decoders, not Unicode normalizers, except Boost.Text (C++, also claims to beat ICU on NFC). Pick unicode-transforms over ICU (or Boost.Text) specifically when you're in a pure-Haskell codebase doing decomposition (NFD/NFKD) and want to remove the ICU4C runtime dependency; for NFC/NFKC-heavy or non-Haskell workloads, ICU or Boost.Text is likely still faster.
verified_claims_summary: The README's per-file wall-clock ms table (package v0.3.7) compares unicode-transforms against text-icu 0.x calling ICU4C 65.1, across 7 language corpora, on unstated macOS hardware (no CPU model, GHC version, or compiler flags given). unicode-transforms wins all 14 NFD/NFKD rows (+8.8% to +376.9%, e.g. NFKD/Korean 7.78ms vs ICU's 37.10ms) but loses 9 of 14 NFC/NFKC rows, including NFC/Japanese (11.90ms vs ICU's 3.04ms) and NFC/AllChars (9.72ms vs 3.58ms).
status_note: Actively maintained — last master commit 2026-01-18, adding support for newer GHC releases up through 9.14; BSD-3-Clause and small enough to vendor, but stability is marked 'Experimental' and there is an open correctness bug in NFKC on Korean text (issue #106).
